Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

supplement 0.0.0.9000

  • check_supplement() now gives a "report-name" row for a report in analyses/ whose name is not valid UTF-8 text, which a file system on Linux can hold. The row says to rename the report. Before, in a UTF-8 locale, the check gave such a report no row. On Linux, Quarto 1.10.19 rendered a site with such a report with no error and left the report out of docs/.

  • On Windows, render_supplement() now publishes the figures that knitr saves from code chunks for a site folder whose path holds an 8.3 short name, such as JANEDO~1. Quarto run from such a path left them out of docs/, and check_supplement() reported broken links. For a path with ~, the function now runs Quarto from the folder’s long path. The site guide tells authors who render in a terminal on Windows to open it in the long path.

  • check_supplement() now reads the links of a page with a large comment or large element text, such as a large htmlwidget. Such a page gave a row saying that its markup goes past the limits of the PCRE pattern engine, which stopped release_supplement(). It held for script, style, textarea, or title text with millions of <, and for a comment with millions of -. It also held for script text with millions of </ or <!, or, after <!--, millions of <s or of separate -. One tag with millions of attributes can still give that row.

  • check_supplement() now resolves the links of a page that has a <base> tag against the base’s href, and no longer reads that href as a link. The help page lists the cases where this differs from a browser. Under such a base, a link of only a # or ? part points to the base address. If no file is there, the link gives a row. A base can have a scheme other than data: or javascript:, such as https:, or start with /. Then the page’s relative links are not checked. Comments now also end at <!-->, <!--->, and --!>. </ followed by a character that is not an ASCII letter or > starts a bogus comment. An end tag is read to its closing >. Links inside either are not read. A script can hold <!-- and then <script>. If no --> comes before the next </script>, the script now runs past it, as in a browser.

  • A site can now be published with the R console, a web browser, and the Git pane of RStudio or Positron, with no GitHub command-line tool. release_supplement() prints and returns four git commands, git status -- ., git add -A -- ., git commit -m "Release vX.Y.Z" -- ., and git push, and no longer prints git tag or gh release create. After them it prints the address of GitHub’s new-release form. The address fills in the tag and the current branch, so GitHub tags the branch that holds the release. It reads the repository from the push address of the origin remote, in the https, http, ssh, or scp-like <user>@github.com: form. When origin is not a GitHub address, it prints the steps on the repository’s Releases page. When git knows the default branch of origin (refs/remotes/origin/HEAD) and the current branch is another one, it says so. When you publish the release, GitHub makes the tag. So push first, and publish right after the push. check_tools() no longer reports gh. The publishing guide sets up git, the GitHub sign-in, the repository, and GitHub Pages with usethis. It renders with render_supplement(). Its last part gives the terminal commands. usethis is a suggested package.

  • New render_supplement() renders a site from the R console. With no arguments it runs quarto render in the site folder. With report names, such as render_supplement("models"), it first renders each report by name, which runs its code again, and then the whole site. When the full render leaves a file of figures/ out of docs/figures/, it renders the whole site once more. It runs the Quarto copy that check_tools() reports, also one that is only inside RStudio or Positron. It runs no git command. A report name must match its file’s letter case. The messages of create_supplement(), add_report(), and check_tools() name it. So do the template’s GUIDE.md and the steps in the rows of check_supplement() that render a changed report again.

  • The home page lists reports in the order of the Analyses menu, when each report has an order from add_report() or the template. The template’s example report has order: 1 in its front matter. add_report() gives each new report the next whole number after the largest order in analyses/. The home page’s table lists reports with an order first, by that number, and the others after them by title. In a site made earlier, whose reports have no order, add_report() writes none, and the table keeps listing reports by title.

  • The package site has a demo, at https://jmgirard.github.io/supplement/demo/: a supplement for a made-up diary study of sleep and next-day mood. The package site’s build makes it with create_supplement(), add_data(), and add_report(), and stops unless check_supplement() finds no problem in it. The README and the site’s navbar link it.

  • check_supplement() has a new argument, renv_lock. With renv_lock = TRUE, it compares the R and package versions that print_environment() prints into each report’s stored output with the site’s renv.lock. A report with a version that differs gets a "renv-mismatch" row, which names the versions and says how to make them match. A report that attached a package that renv.lock does not name, so that renv::restore() does not install it from renv.lock, gets a "renv-missing" row. A package that a report loaded and did not attach gives no row. RENV_PROFILE or renv/profile can name an renv profile. Then these checks read the profile’s lockfile, renv/profiles/<name>/renv.lock, in place of renv.lock. Where the file system ignores letter case, the lockfile can be listed under another spelling, such as Renv.lock. It then gets a "renv-mismatch" row that says to rename it. The default is FALSE, which does not read renv.lock, and release_supplement() does not run these checks.

  • check_supplement() has a new argument, web_links. With web_links = TRUE, it requests each http and https address on the pages in docs/. An address whose request fails, or that gives a status of 400 or above, gets a "web-link" row. For status 401, 403, 405, or 429, the row says that the link can still work in a browser. The default is FALSE, which makes no web request, and release_supplement() does not run this check.

  • The package now needs R 4.1.0 or later.

  • check_supplement() gives the "placeholder" row for the example report of an earlier version of the template, so a site made before the example last changed still gets it. An unchanged example file also gets the row after an editor saves it with small changes. These are a UTF-8 byte order mark at its start, CR line ends, or no line break at its end.

  • Reports now share their setup code through one file in the site, _scripts/report.R, which the template ships. It defines save_png(), which saves a figure in figures/, and print_environment(), which prints the Computing environment section. The last line of each report’s site chunk reads the file: source(file.path(site, "_scripts", "report.R"), local = TRUE). So a report from add_report() no longer holds the Computing environment code, and the example report no longer defines save_png(). The reports still call no supplement function. When a site made earlier has no _scripts/report.R, add_report() copies the template’s file into it, and it never replaces a file that is there. Older reports keep their own code and still render. After a change to _scripts/report.R, render each report by name to take the change.

  • print_environment() in _scripts/report.R ends the Computing environment section with a line that gives the MD5 of the file, with each CR LF read as LF. If the stored output of a report directly in analyses/ gives another MD5 than the site’s _scripts/report.R has now, check_supplement() gives a "stale-script" row. So release_supplement() stops before it releases that output. A report whose stored output gives no MD5, such as one rendered before the site had this version of the file, gets no row.

  • If the site has no _scripts/report.R file and a report directly in analyses/ names it, as the template’s source() line does, check_supplement() gives a "missing-script" row. So release_supplement() stops before it releases reports whose render can fail. If a site made before the template had the file has reports that do not name it, check_supplement() gives no row.

  • The help pages, the guide “Publish a supplement site”, and this news file are built into a pkgdown website for https://jmgirard.github.io/supplement/, which DESCRIPTION’s URL field lists first.

  • A new site’s README.md is now a short page for the people who read the site’s repository: the citation, the site address, the contents, and the licenses. The guide for the site’s authors is a separate file, GUIDE.md. Its rules for edge cases sit in a “Reference” part at its end. When the folder already has a README.md, the first render keeps it and no SUPPLEMENT.md is written. Sites made earlier keep their guide. To add the new guide to such a site, copy system.file("template", "GUIDE.md", package = "supplement") into it, and replace OWNER and REPO in its example figure address. Such a site keeps the old guide until its authors replace it. If its folder had no README.md before the first render, the old guide is README.md. If the folder had a README.md and no SUPPLEMENT.md, the old guide is SUPPLEMENT.md.

  • The template’s .gitignore now holds the lines that Quarto 1.10 adds to a .gitignore that lacks them. A new site’s .gitignore no longer changes on its second render, unless an env/ folder in the site folder holds a Python environment. The template also ignores Quarto’s _*.local files in the site folder, such as _environment.local, which hold settings for one computer. Sites made earlier need no change, because Quarto adds the lines it needs to their .gitignore itself.

  • The template’s two project scripts are now Lua files, _scripts/setup.lua and _scripts/nojekyll.lua, that Quarto runs through Pandoc, so a render starts no Deno process for them. On macOS, Quarto’s Deno sometimes crashed while it ran the old TypeScript scripts, and the render then failed. To switch a site made earlier, copy setup.lua and nojekyll.lua from system.file("template", "_scripts", package = "supplement") into its _scripts/ folder. Change the pre-render and post-render lines of _quarto.yml to name them, and delete setup.ts and nojekyll.ts.

  • Initial package with a Quarto website template for supplemental materials in inst/template/.

  • The template’s home page reads the paper title, citation, and contact from _supplement.yml. A Quarto extension in the template adds three shortcodes: supplement-doi shows a Zenodo DOI badge, supplement-download links to the Zenodo archive, and supplement-data-table lists the data files with their sizes and download links. A data file that does not exist stops the render.

  • create_supplement() makes a new site folder from the template without the Quarto command-line interface. With repo = "owner/name", it also writes the GitHub repository into the site’s links. If the folder already holds a file that the template writes, it stops and writes nothing.

  • check_tools() reports whether Quarto, knitr, rmarkdown, and git are installed, and lists the GitHub and Zenodo accounts that a site needs. It finds Quarto on the system path, in QUARTO_PATH, or in the copy that RStudio or Positron installs. It reports a copy that is not on the system path or is older than Quarto 1.4.0. It runs none of the tools. create_supplement() names each tool that is missing, too old, or not on the system path in its closing message.

  • The template’s home page lists the reports in analyses/ through a Quarto listing, with the title and the description from the front matter of each report, in place of a hand-written table.

  • add_report() writes a new report file in analyses/ and adds it to the Analyses menu in _quarto.yml. add_data() copies a data file into data/ and adds it to the data list in _supplement.yml. Both functions add lines as text, so the comments in these files stay. Both refuse names that Windows reserves for a device, such as con, in any letter case. add_data() also refuses such a name with an extension, such as con.csv, and a file name that ends in ..

  • The template guide, GUIDE.md, has a part on recording a site’s R packages with renv: renv::init(), renv::snapshot() after a render, and renv::restore() on another machine. In a site set up with renv, a full render from stored output still runs no R. check_supplement() finds no problem in the files that renv adds, and git keeps renv/library/ out.

  • write_dockerfile() reads the R and renv versions in the site’s renv lockfile and writes a Dockerfile that builds an image with that R, the packages in the lockfile, and a given Quarto version. The lockfile is renv.lock, unless RENV_PROFILE or renv/profile names an renv profile. Then it is the profile’s lockfile, renv/profiles/<name>/renv.lock, and the image sets RENV_PROFILE to the name. The name can hold only ASCII letters, digits, ., _, and -, and cannot start with .. Another name gives the error class supplement_error_profile. The lockfile must record R 4.0.0 or later and renv 1.3.1 or later. It must not give R, Packages, R.Version, Packages.renv, or Packages.renv.Version twice in one object. The function also writes a .dockerignore that lets only the lockfile of the site’s files into the image. digest pins the base image. The template guide shows how to build the image and render a report in it.

  • check_supplement() lists the problems in a site before a release, and changes no file. It finds files larger than 100 MiB, and saved R objects that git tracks or does not ignore. It finds reports with code and no stored output, and a missing docs/ folder. A code chunk of any engine counts, such as {bash} or {sql}, but not {ojs}, {mermaid}, or {dot}. It counts in any letter case, with a space or tab before {, and inside a > block quote. If the report’s front matter sets engine: knitr, inline R code also counts: r and a space, r#, or {r} and a space after the first backtick. From the source hash that Quarto stores, it finds reports whose stored output was made from other text than the report holds now. A change in a file that the report includes does not count. It also finds stored output whose hash cannot be read. If a hash cannot be read, the row names each such file. Otherwise it names each file whose hash differs. If another file’s hash then matches the report, the row adds a hint. The hint says that the files that differ can be from a dropped format, such as docx. If so, the author deletes them, renders the whole site, and commits the report with _freeze/, docs/, and figures/. The row for a hash that cannot be read adds a delete step. If the row stays after the render steps, the author deletes the named files and renders the whole site. Then the author commits the report with _freeze/, docs/, and figures/. Each named file stands between double quotes, so a name that holds , reads as one file. It finds folders in _freeze/analyses/ that no file or folder in analyses/ names, as after a report is deleted or renamed. It also finds relative links in docs/ to files that are not in docs/, and pages there that cannot be read. It finds files in figures/, docs/, and _freeze/ that git ignores, which a release leaves out. It finds figures in figures/ whose copy in docs/figures/ is missing or differs. The rows for missing, old, or unreadable stored output and for such figures give the steps to render and commit the fix. The hint above and the row for unreadable stored output also give a delete step. The row for a report with no stored output also says: if you added the report to the Analyses menu, as add_report() does, commit _quarto.yml too. It finds DOIs that differ from _supplement.yml, and a CITATION.cff that cannot be read. It finds the template’s placeholder values that the author did not replace. These are the paper title, citation, contact, and authors in _supplement.yml, OWNER/REPO in the GitHub link, and OWNER and REPO in the site address. They are also the “Before your first commit” box, the YEAR AUTHORS copyright lines, and the example report and data while they are unchanged. Each such row stops release_supplement(). It returns the problems as a data frame.

  • release_supplement() prepares a release. An empty citation is one value that stops write_citation() or write_zenodo(). If _supplement.yml holds such a value, the release stops before check_supplement() runs, with an error of the same class and message. If CITATION.cff or .zenodo.json is a folder or a link, it also stops before check_supplement() runs. It then runs check_supplement(). When that finds a problem or skips its git checks, the function stops. If _supplement.yml, CITATION.cff, or .zenodo.json changes while the check runs, the function stops and writes none of these files. A file made or removed counts as a change. The change that you saved then stays in the file. A change saved after the function reads the files again can still be lost. A DOI in CITATION.cff that differs from _supplement.yml does not stop it. It then raises the version in _supplement.yml by "patch", "minor", or "major", or sets a given greater version. It writes CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json again with the new version. It prints the git commands that commit and push the release, and runs none of them. The printed git status, git add, and git commit commands end in -- .. So git add and git commit stage and commit only files under the site folder. This is also true for a site in a subfolder of its repository. If a write stops, the files get their old text back. The commands are printed after the files are written, so an error while printing keeps the files.

  • write_citation() and write_zenodo() write CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json from _supplement.yml. Like write_dockerfile(), they refuse a link at the output path even with overwrite = TRUE, because a write follows the link. On Windows they also refuse a file link to a missing file, and so does release_supplement(). supplement now imports the fs package to find such a link there.

  • The template’s page footer shows the licenses in license.code and license.content of _supplement.yml, in place of a fixed MIT and CC BY 4.0. A new supplement-license shortcode shows a readable name for common ids, such as CC BY 4.0 for CC-BY-4.0, and any other id as written. Each name links to https://spdx.org/licenses/<id>.html in place of links to LICENSE.md and LICENSE-CC-BY.md. SPDX keeps that page only for ids on its license and exception lists. A license value that is not one SPDX id stops the render. Examples are CC BY 4.0, GPL--3.0, and a list. A call also stops the render unless it has one argument, code or content, and no named argument.

  • The supplement-doi badge removes the prefixes in front of a DOI that write_citation() removes: doi:, and http:// or https:// with doi.org/, dx.doi.org/, or www.doi.org/. A DOI written as such a doi.org address no longer breaks the badge. A zenodo.version-doi or zenodo.concept-doi value that write_citation() refuses, such as doi: alone, stops the render.

  • write_citation() stops with supplement_error_license for a license.code or license.content value that does not have the shape of an SPDX id. An id is letters and digits, with one . or - between groups and at most one + at the end. Examples of other values are CC BY 4.0 with spaces and GPL--3.0 with two hyphens in a row. write_zenodo() does the same for license.content, and the footer’s supplement-license shortcode uses the same rule. When the two ids differ only in letter case, CITATION.cff holds one of them.

  • The template’s _supplement.yml has a version field for the site version, such as "1.0.0". When it is not empty, write_citation() and write_zenodo() write it. They stop for a value that is not three whole numbers joined by ., or that has a leading zero.

  • Authors in the template’s _supplement.yml now have family: and given: in place of name:. Both functions stop with an error for an author without them.

  • When a write fails, create_supplement(), add_report(), and add_data() remove only the files and folders that they made. Before, these functions read [, *, and ? in a site path as a pattern. For a site path such as site[ab], the cleanup then removed files in another folder, such as sitea, and kept its own.

  • A _supplement.yml or _quarto.yml that the yaml package cannot read now gives an error of class supplement_error_parse. Examples are a [ or a { that is not closed and a key given twice. The message names the file and gives the message of the yaml package, and no file changes. write_citation(), write_zenodo(), check_supplement(), release_supplement(), and add_data() give it for _supplement.yml, and add_report() gives it for _quarto.yml. Before, the first four gave the yaml package’s own error. add_data() and add_report() gave supplement_error_yaml, the class for a changed file that does not read back as planned. For a key line indented with a tab, add_data() gave supplement_error_no_data_list.

  • The template publishes paper figures from a figures/ folder, which git tracks. The template ships figures/bootstrap-means.png, so the first render of a new site publishes it. The example report saves it again on each render that runs its code. The example finds the site folder in a site chunk. If QUARTO_PROJECT_DIR is not empty, as in a render, the chunk uses it. Otherwise the chunk looks for _quarto.yml in the current folder first, then in the folder above it, and uses the first folder that holds it. If neither holds it, the chunk stops with a message. So the example also works with execute-dir: project and with its code run by hand from the site folder or from analyses/. A failed plot leaves no partial file in figures/. A PNG file that does not end with the PNG end chunk, such as one that a full disk cut short, also leaves none. When its code runs, the report stops with a message if a file named figures is in place of the folder. If figures is a link, or on Windows a junction, the report also stops. The template guide, GUIDE.md, says how a report writes a figure to figures/. In new sites, git ignores .png and .pdf files saved directly in analyses/ in any letter case.

  • The template’s example report and each report that add_report() writes end with a “Computing environment” section. It prints the R and package versions of the render. If the sessioninfo package is installed, it uses sessioninfo::session_info(). Otherwise it uses utils::sessionInfo(). It shows the home folder as ~, and folders outside it in full. The stored output keeps the versions of each report’s last render.

  • In each report that add_report() writes, the first code chunk is the example report’s site chunk, so the report finds the site folder by the same rule. Its text says to read a data file as file.path(site, "data", "<file name>"). Before, its text said to read data from ... That path is wrong for code run from the site folder. The template guide, GUIDE.md, tells reports to read fit files as file.path(site, "analyses", "fits", ...). In a site made before this change, copy the site chunk from a new site’s analyses/example.qmd into each report.

  • Fixes on Windows. create_supplement(), add_report(), and add_data() now stop with supplement_error_file_exists for a junction where the site needs a folder, as they already did on other systems for a link. Before, they wrote through the junction into the folder it points to. The data table shortcode shows the size of a data file of 2 GiB or more. Before, it showed “-1 B”. When git lists a file name that is not valid UTF-8, check_supplement() no longer stops with an error.

  • check_supplement() now reads links from start tags only. Before, it also read link-shaped text in comments, in <script> and <style> text, and in page text such as <code>. It also read attributes such as data-href, and it reported those as broken links. It now decodes character references such as &amp;, so a link to R&D.csv written as R&amp;D.csv is no longer reported. It reads HREF and other letter cases (also in xlink:href) and unquoted values, and it removes the spaces at the ends of a link. The help page lists the main cases that it still reads differently from a browser.

  • check_supplement() now reads pages in hidden folders of docs/ and hidden pages, such as docs/.page.html. It does not enter a linked folder. Before, a symbolic link in docs/ to a folder there repeated the rows of each page in that folder. A link to docs/ itself repeated them many times. A symbolic link in docs/ to an existing file or folder outside docs/ now gives a broken-link row. The published site does not have its target. On Windows, a junction in docs/ to a folder outside docs/ also gives that row. A link on a page that goes through such a link also gives a row.

  • Package functions read YAML files without running !expr code, also when options(yaml.eval.expr = TRUE) is set. Such a value is read as the text of its R code.

  • New guide, vignette("publishing"): the steps from an empty folder to a site on GitHub Pages with a Zenodo DOI. It also gives the rule for rendering again after a report changes: render the report by name, render the whole site, then commit the report with _freeze/, docs/, and figures/.

Developed by Jeffrey M. Girard.
